explanation:
The mismatch is a tie‑break problem, not a rule problem. In pair 2 the bottom block has a 1×2 hole, and two 1×2 pieces exist: the 6‑pair at (2,7..8) and a pair of 7s at (0,8..9). My code took the first in reading order (the 7s), but the expected output moves the 6s. The 7s are the scattered noise colour of that pair (it appears as four separate objects), while the 6 piece is the only object of its colour – just as the 3, 9, 8, 2 pieces in the other pairs are each the sole object of their colour, and the noise colours (6, 4) are splintered into several objects. So the pieces to move are the objects whose colour occurs exactly once; noise colours are never moved even if a fragment happens to fit a hole. In the test input the noise colour 2 appears as seven single cells, while 7 and 4 are unique, consistent with this.

Correction: restrict matching to objects whose colour has exactly one object, falling back to the rest only if nothing unique matches.
